samples.identification: Atom's Connections 1.7.1 beta, unsigned .NET loopback application
evidence: Inspected all 17 managed methods, starting at Main token 0x06000001; Run launches a browser via UseShellExecute=true and listens on loopback port 47800 by default.

LoadFiles token 0x06000005 validates app.pak SHA256 db2fd6b4dc620bdddf8cad94e451514066e9cd8181f40ba9a4905159800ccc3c, decompresses GZip, and reads three length-prefixed web assets. No native or managed executable is reconstructed.

Handle token 0x06000006 checks Host and Sec-Fetch-Site; device-key and save require POST plus X-Atoms. SafeTarget token 0x06000009 rejects traversal, reserved names and paths outside Pictures/Documents application subdirectories.

DPAPI protects a newly generated 32-byte device key, not harvested credentials. WMI/Process.Kill targets another copy of the same image on the same port after bind failure. Registry writes install an atoms: URL handler; the shortcut is on the Desktop, not a startup trigger.

Recovered 10979 JavaScript decoder calls using only the isolated string-table decoder and rotation. Application code was not executed. Code implements PBKDF2/AES-GCM/ECDH encrypted local storage and authenticated peer sessions, user messaging, attachments and browser-permission camera/microphone calls.
Bundled PeerJS 1.5.4 is byte-identical to upstream distribution: ad5d8870d1e389914f9cba8d35be313c4327c69ee0a221e482e9bf7621136fe5.

Fetched the live publisher site, version.json, portable release, PeerJS endpoint and plugin catalog. The live version is newer (1.11.0), so its different executable hash does not authenticate this historical sample.

Fetched both current catalog plugins and verified their catalog SHA256 values; inspected arithmetic/arcade code and plugin bridge. Plugins run in allow-scripts sandboxed blob iframes with connect-src none. Updates are user-offered downloads, not silent program execution.
samples.assessment: Observed functions fit a private messaging application. Unsigned packaging, compressed assets, JavaScript string-table obfuscation, DPAPI and process-control capabilities plausibly explain generic Trojan detections. No theft or operator command channel was found. Publisher attribution is unauthenticated and original delivery context is missing; BENIGN is quarantine triage, not a known-good trust assertion.

samples.identification: XMRig 6.26.0 official static Linux x86-64 image with 64-byte trailer
evidence: Downloaded official v6.26.0 linux-static-x64 release. Archive SHA256 fc6f8ae5f64e4f17481f7e3be29a1c56949f216a998414188003eae1db20c9e5 matches the upstream release checksum.

All 8350992 bytes of upstream xmrig (SHA256 b20f39fc00d242e706b6c30367ad811c676e0575050a4ec2f30104b696944b49) match the beginning of this 8351056-byte sample. Only 64 trailing bytes differ; they are beyond every ELF section and load segment.
Rizin entry 0x40e5f3 reaches main 0x40d280. Main dispatches CLI handling at 0x458c60 or constructs/runs the application at 0x501040/0x501650. The no-valid-config path at 0x5017a0 returns status 2.

Compared the unchanged image and configuration flow with upstream Base.cpp: command-line inputs, data-directory config.json, ~/.xmrig.json and ~/.config/xmrig.json supply mining configuration. No supplied wallet, pool configuration or deployment script accompanies this sample.

Reviewed decoded facts: recovered stack HTTP headers and proof-of-work fields are consistent with the stock miner; URL decoding of printf formats and XOR/hex interpretations do not supply a hidden command or payload.
samples.assessment: The systemd-ntpd name and hostile feed provenance are concerning and suggest possible unauthorized deployment of a legitimate miner. Mining detections fit XMRig; Mirai attribution is unsupported by the unchanged official image. The unexplained trailer is not loaded as code and is not authenticated. Without launcher, configuration, persistence or operator-consent evidence, unauthorized mining is not established. Retain accurate mining and naming traits; BENIGN routes to quarantine, not trusted benign.

trait_changes.matcher_fix: dotnet-sha256-reference now recognizes the unqualified CLR SHA256 type name as well as provider variants; remains notable and describes a reference.
trait_changes.placement: Cryptographic provider names/API references do not prove dynamic-library loading. Relocated matchers retain their original type/platform/criticality/confidence. Updated direct consumers. crypto-library-context retains EVP membership in the old crypto/library selector; network-lib-marker retains libcrypto membership in dylib/library; ssl-lib-targets explicitly retains its former moved member.

checks.atomscan_rerun: Both target SHAs confirmed with the edited traits. Neither target emits hostile or suspicious YAML traits. SHA256 reference fires for the PE; both relocated provider references fire for the ELF.
checks.scope_note: Provider atoms retain unix/windows scripts/binaries scope. Ancestor-group retention controls exercise PE scope. Legacy crypto-library-context retains its existing linux/macos/windows binary scope.
